preconditions: vertical and lateral directions recorded separately
interval-boundary and regular-grid sampling modes not mixed
logic: Fit transition matrices independently by environment/process and validate by holding out entire regions.
requiredEvidence: at least three independent regions per environment/process group
uncertainty: Dirichlet smoothing prevents zero estimates but never authorizes unseen facies or environments.
exclusions: using transition probabilities as deterministic stratigraphic order
inferring lateral continuity from vertical logs alone
reopenCondition: A multi-region normalized observed corpus is assembled

claimBindings.statement: Fit transition matrices independently by environment/process and validate by holding out entire regions.

sourceLocators.locator: Carle, Fogg and Gaetan (1998), Conditional Simulation of Hydrofacies, abstract: transition-probability/Markov approach represents spatial cross-correlation, juxtapositional tendencies, proportions, anisotropy and three-dimensional Markov chains

Weissmann, Carle and Fogg (1999), abstract: lateral mean lengths and transition probabilities from soil maps are combined with a separate vertical transition chain from well data; the resulting 3D model represents cross-correlation and asymmetry including fining-upward tendencies
USGS SIR 2008-5035, T-PROGS methods section; retained as a public workflow example only. Precise page-level locator remains pending because this source was not reopened in cycle 101

claimBindings.applicability: All stated preconditions and required evidence must be satisfied
exclusions: using transition probabilities as deterministic stratigraphic order
inferring lateral continuity from vertical logs alone
claimBindings.verificationNote: Cycle 101 verified the two primary article abstracts and an independent USGS application. This supports the direction/environment separation and cross-correlation concepts, but not a universal transition matrix or any numeric probability.
